identity.real_world_identity_notes: Caterham Seven Supersport, a road-going Seven with a Ford Sigma 1.6 and a five-speed gearbox with sprint ratios, also raced in the one-make Supersport championship.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. No automatic cut or blip was present, so the driver supplies the upshift lift.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.
Confidence is medium because the construction of the five-speed is inferred rather than stated. A source showing a dog-engagement box in this specification would make the downshift blip required.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.caterham-supersport.20260814t042002848z-540349d0 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: Registered sources establish the Supersport variant and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

Wikipedia lists the Supersport with a Caterham-Ford Sigma engine and Seven transmissions as five-speed manual, six-speed manual and six-speed sequential manual; the live drive selected five H-pattern gears, which is the non-sequential five-speed. Construction is inferred from the road-going five-speed manual rather than stated by a source.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: The Seven is offered with a five-speed manual, a six-speed manual and a six-speed sequential; the drive selected the five-speed manual. Probably synchronised, so the blip eases it but should not be needed to engage the gear.
